privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data Librishelf processes, why, and how you control it.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: Account data: username, email and password. Your password is stored securely and nobody can read it, not even us.

Content you add: your books and their details (title, authors, publisher, ISBN, series, tags, dates, ratings, reading status and goals), personal notes and the covers you upload. Personal notes are yours only: they never appear in your public library.
Access data: the IP address of your visits is used briefly, only to protect the service from abuse such as repeated login attempts.

sections.title: How we use it
paragraphs: Only to run Librishelf: keep you signed in, store and show your library, and protect your account.
We do not sell or share your data with anyone, and we use no advertising or tracking tools.

sections.title: Public library
paragraphs: Your library is private by default. If you turn on sharing in Account, anyone with your link can see your books and covers, and some covers may appear on the site's sign-in pages.
You can turn it off whenever you want, and the change is immediate.
Public libraries don't show up in search engines like Google: the site asks for them not to be indexed.

sections.title: Community and followers
paragraphs: Both options start off and live in Account. "Join the community" (only with a public library) lets other signed-in readers see that you have the same book, your rating for it and how many books you share.

"Accept followers" lets other people ask to follow you. Only those you approve see, in their feed, the books you add and finish. You can remove followers or turn the option off at any time, and the change takes effect immediately.
You can block a reader from their public library: you stop seeing each other in the community and they can't ask to follow you.

sections.title: ISBN lookup
paragraphs: When you click Look up, Librishelf checks the ISBN on Open Library (openlibrary.org), a public book catalog. The request is made by our server: Open Library only receives the ISBN, never your data or your account.

sections.title: Emails we send
paragraphs: We use your email only for account matters: confirming the address when you sign up and sending a password recovery link when you ask for one. We don't send marketing.
Links are short-lived (1 hour for passwords, 3 days for confirmation), work only once, and we store only a hashed version of them.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We use a single essential cookie that keeps you signed in. It is not used for tracking or advertising.
Your theme and language preferences are saved only in your browser.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: For as long as your account exists. When you delete your account, all your data is removed immediately.
Backups may keep this data for a limited period until they are replaced.

sections.title: Your rights (LGPD)
paragraphs: You can view, correct, download a copy of or delete your data at any time, all from the app: in Account → Your data you download everything as JSON or CSV, and deleting your account erases everything right away. For any other request, contact us below.
